newsitem.title: USA: Illinois comptroller unveils accounting system.
newsitem.headline: Illinois comptroller unveils accounting system.

text.p: Illinois Comptroller Loleta Didrickson on Monday said her office would unveil a computerized accounting system this week that provide access to state spending information through the Internet.

The $14.5 million Statewide Accounting Management System is scheduled to go on line Tuesday. It will replace 23-year-old equipment, address the so-called Year 2000 bug and provide online access to the comptroller's voluminous records, Didrickson said.

The system will also make it possible by the middle of next year for Illinois to process invoices electronically and eliminate 85 redundant systems. That could save the state $125 million outright and another $25 million annually if other agencies go along with it, Didrickson said.

American Management Systems provided financial software for the system, which has been in development for 13 months, Didrickson said. Illinois is the largest of the Fairfax, Virginia-based company's 18 state government clients.
Internet access to state spending records is the most unique aspect of this project, Caroline Rapking, a vice president of American Management, said Monday.
"Illinois will be the only state to have this depth of information available over the Internet at this point," Rapking said.

Most states provide access to static information, but the comptroller's system provides a query engine that will allow a viewer to probe state contracts from a particular vendor by department and total amount, Rapking said.

Didrickson said American Management was selected through competitive bidding for $8.1 million. International Business Machines Corp built the database for $3.5 million and a consulting firm received another $1.9 million.

Didrickson said the state saved $4.5 million in recoding costs with the Year 2000 compatible system. It could save up to $137 million more if other agencies use the comptroller's software rather than recoding their own systems to eliminate the Year 2000 bug, arising from the inability of some systems to read dates after 1999 correctly.
Beginning Tuesday, the new linc.net program can be found through the comptroller's World Wide Web site at http://www.comptroller.state.il.us.
